newsitem.title: ITALY: Omnitel sees 1996 loss around 600 bln lire.
newsitem.headline: Omnitel sees 1996 loss around 600 bln lire.

text.p: Italy's mobile phone consortium Omnitel, in which Olivetti has a 35.5 percent stake, expects to post 1996 losses of around 600 billion lire, managing director Silvio Scaglia said on Tuesday.
Scaglia, talking to reporters while attending a business conference, reiterated that Omnitel had 713,000 subscribers by end-1996. It began operating in December 1995.
"The aim is to double this number in 1997," Scaglia said.

Referring to a 60 billion lire compensation sum for a reduction in connection fees which state telecoms holding Stet is to pay Omnitel, he said one quarter of this would impact 1996 accounts and the rest 1997 accounts.
Omnitel, which reported a net loss of 260 billion lire in the first half of 1996, has said it aims to break even in 1998.

Omnitel had complained to the European Commission about a 750 billion lire licence fee it was forced to pay when it started up. Italy's other mobile phone group TIM, majority owned by Stet, did not have to pay such a fee.
